description: Shopping assistant with order search, delivery tracking, and return-window tools.

tools.name: search_orders
tools.description: Search the user's order history. Returns orders whose placement timestamp falls in [ordered_after, ordered_before). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); ordered_after is inclusive, ordered_before is exclusive.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text item or brand filter (optional; empty returns all orders in range)

tools.name: get_next_delivery
tools.description: Return the user's next incoming delivery: the shipment with the soonest estimated arrival, including its estimated arrival timestamp (eta_utc, UTC ISO 8601).

tools.name: get_delivery_status
tools.description: Return the shipment status for one order (carrier, status, and UTC ISO 8601 timestamps such as shipped_utc / delivered_utc / eta_utc where applicable).

tools.name: get_return_window
tools.description: Return the return-window deadline for one order as return_by_utc (UTC ISO 8601). Returns postmarked after this instant are rejected.

scenarios.title: orders-last-30-days
scenarios.user: How many orders have I placed in the last 30 days?

checks.note: Jun 25, Jul 5, Jul 18 rows; the Jun 20 row predates every admissible start

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 23 2026, 6:30pm EDT (UTC-4) = 2026-07-23T22:30Z. Day-grain 'last 30 days' admits the exact sliding window now-30d..now = [2026-06-23T22:30Z, 2026-07-23T22:30Z) (this is what nl2time returns) and calendar-day variants: 30 calendar days ending today = Jun 24 00:00 ET..Jul 24 00:00 ET = [2026-06-24T04:00Z, 2026-07-24T04:00Z); day-floored start with either end (Jun 23 00:00 ET = 04:00Z start; end = now or end of today Jul 24 00:00 ET = 04:00Z). Rows deliberately avoid Jun 23-24 (the disputed start days) and today, so every admissible tuple selects exactly the same 3 rows: Jun 25 (1:30pm EDT), Jul 5, Jul 18. The Jun 20 row (33 days back) is outside all readings. Trap-free baseline scenario.

scenarios.title: last-weekend-orders
scenarios.user: What did I order last weekend?

checks.note: Sunday-evening yoga mat (UTC Monday) must be included; Friday-night phone case (UTC Saturday) and the Jul 6 water filter must not
Saturday-afternoon shoes order must be included

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 15 2026, 9:30am CDT (UTC-5) — midweek, so 'last weekend' is unambiguously the just-past Sat-Sun: Sat Jul 11 00:00 CT..Mon Jul 13 00:00 CT = [2026-07-11T05:00Z, 2026-07-13T05:00Z), which nl2time confirms. Double UTC trap: the yoga mat (2026-07-13T00:40Z) is Sunday Jul 12, 7:40pm CDT — inside — though its UTC day is Monday; the phone case (2026-07-11T02:30Z) is Friday Jul 10, 9:30pm CDT — outside — though its UTC day is Saturday. Naive UTC-day weekend bounds [Jul 11 00Z, Jul 13 00Z) swap exactly those two. Correct contents: trail running shoes (Sat 2:45pm CDT) and yoga mat; water filter (Mon Jul 6) is a range decoy. No count check — a listing answer need not state a number.

scenarios.title: next-delivery-eta-day
scenarios.user: When's my next delivery arriving? What day should I expect it?

checks.note: ETA is Thursday July 9, 8:00pm EDT; the UTC timestamp reads July 10 — answering July 10 fails
If a time is given it must be 8:00 pm local, not midnight

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL. Now = Wednesday Jul 8 2026, 9:00am EDT (UTC-4). get_next_delivery (no time params) returns eta_utc 2026-07-10T00:00:00Z, which in America/New_York is Thursday July 9, 8:00pm — tomorrow local, but the day after tomorrow by UTC calendar day. Correct answers name July 9 (rejectUtcDay is real: UTC day Jul 10 != local day Jul 9). clockTime fires only if a clock time appears; then it must be 8:00pm, not 12:00am (rejectUtcClock real: 00:00 vs 20:00). get_delivery_status is mocked identically and a search_orders row (ordered Jul 6, 10:20am EDT) exists in case the model looks the order up first.

scenarios.title: return-window-closes-midnight
scenarios.user: When does the return window on my headphones order close? What's the last day I can send them back?

checks.note: Deadline is Friday July 31, 11:59pm PDT; the UTC timestamp reads August 1 — answering August 1 fails
If a time is given it must be 11:59 pm local, not 6:59

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL deadline rendering near local midnight and a month boundary. Now = Tuesday Jul 28 2026, 4:45pm PDT (UTC-7). get_return_window returns return_by_utc 2026-08-01T06:59:00Z = Friday July 31, 11:59pm PDT: the last day to ship a return is July 31; the naive UTC reading says August 1 (rejectUtcDay real). Consistent story: delivered 2026-07-01T20:00:00Z (Jul 1, 1:00pm PDT) + 30 days -> end of July 31 local. clockTime is conditional; if quoted it must be 11:59pm, not 6:59 (rejectUtcClock real). search_orders row (ordered Jun 28, 11:30am PDT) provided for order lookup.

scenarios.title: orders-in-may
scenarios.user: How many orders did I place in May?

checks.note: Garden hose, gift wrap, and the May 31 10:30pm string lights; the Apr 30 9pm vacuum filter is out

scenarios.rationale: Now = MONDAY Jun 1 2026, 9:00am EDT — asked just past the month boundary. May 2026 as a civil month in New York (EDT, UTC-4, all month): May 1 00:00 ET..Jun 1 00:00 ET = [2026-05-01T04:00Z, 2026-06-01T04:00Z), confirmed by nl2time. Boundary traps on both ends: the string-lights row (2026-06-01T02:30Z) is Sunday May 31, 10:30pm EDT — inside — though its UTC day is June 1; the vacuum-filter row (2026-05-01T01:00Z) is Thursday April 30, 9:00pm EDT — outside — though its UTC day is May 1. Naive UTC-month bounds [May 1 00Z, Jun 1 00Z) count the filter and drop the lights (still 3, but wrong rows — arg grading catches it); count under correct bounds = 3 (May 10, May 22, May 31).

scenarios.title: shipped-yesterday-sydney

checks.reject: \bno\b|did not ship|didn't ship|hasn't shipped|has not shipped|two days ago|day before yesterday|jul(?:y)?\.? 14\b|\b14th\b|\btuesday\b
checks.note: Shipped Wednesday Jul 15, 8:30am AEST = yesterday. The UTC timestamp reads Tuesday Jul 14 — 'no / two days ago / July 14' are the naive readings
If a time is given it must be 8:30 am local, not 10:30 pm

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL, southern-hemisphere winter. Now = THURSDAY Jul 16 2026, 9:10am AEST (UTC+10 — no DST in July). get_delivery_status returns shipped_utc 2026-07-14T22:30:00Z, which in Sydney is Wednesday July 15, 8:30am — yesterday. Sydney's local day runs AHEAD of UTC: the naive UTC reading says Tuesday July 14, i.e. two days ago, so the naive answer is 'no'. Correct answer: yes (shipped yesterday morning); rejects cover 'no', 'two days ago', 'July 14', and 'Tuesday' (none of which appear in any correct rendering: order placed Monday Jul 13 1:40pm AEST, ETA Friday Jul 17 2:00pm AEST). clockTime conditional: 8:30am local, not the 10:30pm UTC wall clock. get_next_delivery mocked identically; search_orders row provided for lookup.

scenarios.title: past-48-hours-sydney
scenarios.user: How many orders have I placed in the past 48 hours?

checks.note: Kettle (Mon 7pm AEST), charger (Tue 10:30am), doona cover (Tue 11:05pm); the desk fan is 50+ hours back

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Aug 5 2026, 5:20pm AEST (UTC+10) = 2026-08-05T07:20Z. 'Past 48 hours' is an exact sliding window: [now-48h, now) = [2026-08-03T07:20Z, 2026-08-05T07:20Z), confirmed by nl2time. The offset IS the trap: a model that treats the local wall clock as UTC computes [Aug 3 17:20Z, Aug 5 17:20Z), which drops the electric kettle (2026-08-03T09:00Z = Mon Aug 3, 7:00pm AEST — inside the true window, Sydney's local day/evening ahead of UTC) and returns 2. In range: kettle, phone charger (Tue 10:30am AEST), doona cover (2026-08-04T13:05Z = Tue Aug 4, 11:05pm AEST); the desk fan (2026-08-03T05:00Z = Mon 3:00pm AEST) is 50.3 hours before now — outside. Count = 3.

scenarios.title: friday-before-last-kolkata
scenarios.user: How many orders did I place on the Friday before last?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time drops the 'before last' qualifier and resolves the phrase as bare 'Friday' -> most recent Friday Jul 17 (alt: upcoming Friday Jul 24). Golden is the Friday one week earlier, Jul 10 — nl2time issue to file

checks.note: Cricket bat grip (Fri 1:30am IST) + gasket (Fri 12:45pm IST); screen guard is Saturday 1:00am IST and jasmine tea is last Friday

scenarios.rationale: Now = TUESDAY Jul 21 2026, 11:45am IST (UTC+5:30, half-hour offset zone). Last Friday = Jul 17; 'Friday before last' = Friday Jul 10. As a civil day in Kolkata: [Jul 10 00:00 IST, Jul 11 00:00 IST) = [2026-07-09T18:30Z, 2026-07-10T18:30Z) — bounds land at 18:30Z, never midnight UTC. The cricket bat grip (2026-07-09T20:00Z) is Friday Jul 10, 1:30am IST — inside — though its UTC day is Thursday Jul 9; the screen guard (2026-07-10T19:30Z) is Saturday Jul 11, 1:00am IST — outside — though its UTC day is Friday Jul 10. Naive UTC-day bounds [Jul 10 00Z, Jul 11 00Z) swap those two (count still 2 but wrong rows; arg grading catches it). Jasmine tea (Jul 17, 1:30pm IST) is last Friday, not the one before. Count = 2 (grip + gasket, Fri 12:45pm IST).

scenarios.title: orders-in-q2
scenarios.user: How many orders did I place in Q2?

checks.note: Bike tires (Apr 15), picnic blanket (May 20), beach towels (Jun 30 10:10pm EDT); rain jacket was Mar 31 9pm EDT and sunscreen is Jul 2

scenarios.rationale: Now = Saturday Jul 11 2026, 10:05am EDT. Q2 2026 as civil quarter in New York: Apr 1 00:00 ET..Jul 1 00:00 ET = [2026-04-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z) — EDT (UTC-4) applies at both bounds (US spring-forward was Mar 8 2026); nl2time confirms. Boundary traps at both ends: the beach towel set (2026-07-01T02:10Z) is Tuesday Jun 30, 10:10pm EDT — inside Q2 — though its UTC day is Jul 1; the rain jacket (2026-04-01T01:00Z) is Tuesday Mar 31, 9:00pm EDT — Q1, outside — though its UTC day is Apr 1. Naive UTC-quarter bounds count the jacket and drop the towels (still 3, wrong rows — arg grading catches it). Sunscreen (Jul 2, 11:00am EDT) is plainly Q3. Count = 3.

scenarios.title: three-days-ago-order
scenarios.user: What did I order three days ago?

checks.note: Only the Saturday Aug 1 desk lamp; the Aug 2 cable (two days ago) and Jul 30 notebooks (five days ago) are decoys

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline. Now = TUESDAY Aug 4 2026, 11:00am CDT (UTC-5). Three days ago = the civil day Saturday Aug 1 in Chicago: [Aug 1 00:00 CT, Aug 2 00:00 CT) = [2026-08-01T05:00Z, 2026-08-02T05:00Z), confirmed by nl2time. All rows sit mid-day local (desk lamp Sat 12:20pm, HDMI cable Sun 1:00pm, notebooks Thu Jul 30 11:30am) — no UTC/local day divergence anywhere. Correct answer names the desk lamp only.
